paragraphs.en: If you want to tell the history of the whole world, a history that does not privilege one part of humanity, you cannot do it through written {documents} alone, because most of the world, for most of the time, has never had texts to record their emotions, {customs} or history. {Artifacts} , {oral} traditions, {songs} , and other non-literate ( (非文字的) ) forms of expression provide important insights into social practices, while writing is one of humanity's later achievements.Even many {rural} areas where people could not read or write recorded their concerns primarily in objects, and only in writing until fairly recently.
paragraphs.cn: 如果你想讲述全世界的历史，一部不 <u> 偏袒 </u> 人类任何一方的历史，你就不能只通过书面 <u> 文献 </u> 来完成，因为在大部分时间里，世界上大部分地区的人们从未有过文字来记录他们的情感、 <u> 习俗 </u> 或历史。 <u> 人工制品 </u> 、 <u> 口述 </u> 传统、 <u> 歌谣 </u> 及其他非文字形式的表达，为我们深入了解社会习俗提供了重要视角，而文字只是人类后来取得的成就之一。直到最近，在许多人连读写都不会的 <u> 农村 </u> 地区，人们也仍主要通过实物，只是偶尔才会用文字，来记录他们所关注的问题。

paragraphs.en: We might learn a lot about {government} {policies} or {wars} from historical texts, but these sources often miss the personal stories of ordinary people who lived through those events.Ideally, a history would bring together texts and objects, but in many cases this simply can't be done.The clearest example of this is perhaps the first {conflict} , at Botany {Bay} , between {Captain} Cook's {voyage} and the Aboriginal {Australians} .From the {English} side, we have scientific reports and the {military leaders’} record of that {horrible} day.From the Australian side, we have only a {wooden} shield ( (盾) ) dropped by a {soldier} in the fight after his first experience of {gunfire} .If we want to {reconstruct} what was actually going on that day, the shield must be {questioned} and interpreted as deeply and {strictly} as the written reports. {Furthermore} , natural {disasters} like {earthquakes} and {floods} can {destroy} ancient texts, resulting in gaps in our knowledge of the past.
paragraphs.cn: 通过历史文献，我们或许能了解许多关于 <u> 政府政策 </u> 或 <u> 战争 </u> 的信息，但这些资料往往会遗漏许多经历过那些事件的普通人的故事。理想情况下，一部历史应该将文字资料与实物结合起来，但在很多情况下，我们根本无法做到。最典型的例子或许是库克 <u> 船长 </u> 的 <u> 航行 </u> 队伍与 <u> 澳大利亚 </u> 原住民在博特尼 <u> 湾 </u> 发生的首次 <u> 冲突 </u> 。从 <u> 英国人的 </u> 角度，我们有科学报告和 <u> 军事将领 </u> 对那个 <u> 可怕 </u> 日子的记录。而从澳大利亚原住民的角度，我们仅有一面 <u> 木 </u> 盾，那是一名（原住民） <u> 战士 </u> 在战斗中初次遭遇 <u> 炮火 </u> 后掉落的。如果我们想 <u> 重现 </u> 当天的真实情况，就必须跟对待书面报告一样，深入且 <u> 严谨地审视 </u> 和解读这面盾牌。 <u> 此外 </u> ， <u> 地震 </u> 和 <u> 洪水 </u> 等自然 <u> 灾害 </u> 也会 <u> 毁坏 </u> 古代文献，导致我们对过去的认知出现空白。

paragraphs.en: In addition to the problem of {miscomprehension} from both sides, there are {victories} that are {accidentally} or deliberately twisted, especially when only the {victors} know how to write.The {winning} {nation} would {justify} their actions, deciding which parts of the story are emphasized and which are {forgotten} .Those who are {defeated} often have only objects to tell their stories.The Caribbean Taino ( (泰诺人) ), the Aboriginal Australians and other {minority} groups can speak to us of their past achievements most {powerfully} through the objects they made.When we consider contact between literate and non-literate societies such as these, all our {first-hand} accounts are necessarily twisted, only one half of a {dialogue} .If we are to find the other half of that conversation, we have to read not just the texts, but the objects.
paragraphs.cn: 除了双方可能存在的 <u> 误解 </u> 问题，还有一些 <u> 胜利 </u> 是被 <u> 无意 </u> 或有意地歪曲了的，尤其是当只有 <u> 胜利者 </u> 掌握书写能力时。 <u> 获胜的国家 </u> 会为自己的行为 <u> 辩解 </u> ，决定故事的哪些部分要着重强调，哪些部分要被 <u> 遗忘 </u> 。那些 <u> 战败 </u> 者往往只能借助物品讲述他们的故事。加勒比海的泰诺人、澳大利亚原住民及其他 <u> 少数 </u> 族群可以通过他们制作的物品，极 <u> 有力地 </u> 向我们讲述他们往昔的成就。当我们审视像这样有文字的社会和无文字的社会之间的接触时，我们所有的 <u> 一手 </u> 资料必然存在偏差，只展现了 <u> 对话 </u> 的一半内容。如果我们想找到对话的另一半内容，我们不仅要研读文字资料，还要研究那些物品。 5NoOncib/NjiX02BpMIzP4m+378Hw1xTRxUdPaP/PFjKUFq4K2G7tp6ZLYoCE601yW1W39VMdLmovFdSHs4nVQ==
